findings.title: All-clients permission is ignored when an individual client resource exists
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), if resourceStore.findByName finds a resource for the specific client, evaluation proceeds only against that individual resource and never falls back to the 'Clients' resource-type resource. Scope permissions created for the whole Clients resource type with no resources field are associated with the all-resource, not with each client resource. As a result, an admin granted MANAGE, CONFIGURE, or MAP_ROLES for all clients can be denied for a client that happens to have an individual resource (for example because another single-client permission was created). The method must evaluate both the specific client resource and the all-clients resource before deciding.

findings.title: Individual client resources are created without their resource type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates the per-client resource with resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) but never sets the resource type to resourceType. The new ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission relies on resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), which will not find these individual resources. The callback therefore sees only the singleton 'Clients' resource created by init, so getClientsWithPermission cannot return the actual client IDs for per-client grants. The resource type must be set on newly created resources before they are returned.

findings.title: Missing all-clients resource leads to null pointer dereference
findings.body: When the individual client resource is not found, hasPermission(ClientModel, String) obtains the all-clients resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). That method can return null if the 'Clients' resource-type resource does not exist, but the code immediately passes resource to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). A missing or not-yet-initialized all-resource then throws a NullPointerException instead of simply denying the check. A null check is needed before querying policies.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission can return the 'Clients' sentinel instead of client IDs
findings.body: resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) includes the resource-type resource named 'Clients' that represents all clients. If the caller has an all-clients grant for the requested scope, hasGrantedPermission returns true for that resource and the code adds resource.getName(), i.e. 'Clients', to the result set. The method contract returns client IDs, so callers receive a bogus non-client-ID entry and still do not receive the actual clients implied by the all-clients permission. The all-resource must be excluded from this enumeration or expanded into real client IDs.

findings.title: Client removal cleanup is skipped under admin fine-grained authz V2
findings.body: The removal listener is now gated by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), which is the V1 feature. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled instead, ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent never reaches the cleanup branch, and there is no alternative V2 cleanup in this change. Since this PR introduces per-client authorization resources under the admin permissions client, deleting a client that has client-specific scope permissions leaves orphaned Clients resources in the authorization store. A V2-aware cleanup path is needed for client removal.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve the new Clients resource type
findings.body: getResourceName special-cases USERS to resolve a username, but the newly added Clients resource type falls through to return resource.getDisplayName(). Per-client resources created by getOrCreateResource are named with the internal client id and do not have a display name set, so callers get null or an internal UUID rather than the client's clientId. A Clients branch analogous to the Users branch should resolve the client and return its clientId.
